title: Distributed multi-GPU throughput benchmark: tensor+pipeline hybrid profiles
creator: Sofia Patel
description: Purpose: build a repeatable harness and baseline for multi-GPU distributed inference throughput (tokens/sec) across tensor, pipeline, and hybrid parallel configurations. We want p95 latency tracking, tokens/sec scaling curves, and automated regression detection when new runtime changes or kernel swaps alter performance. This work feeds the runtime-2.4 rollout and the dedicated capacity sizing guidance.
test_plan: 1) Reproduce single-node single-GPU baseline with existing microbench harness; 2) Extend harness to orchestrate 2/4/8 GPU runs across multiple nodes using SSH+NCCL + coordinator; 3) Measure steady-state tokens/sec and p95 latency under realistic request shapes (seq_len=256/512/2048), with KV cache warm and cold; 4) Run three parallel topologies: pure tensor-parallel (TP), pure pipeline-parallel (PP), and hybrid (TP+PP); 5) Capture per-step token production, per-request p95, GPU utilization, PCIe/NVLink throughput; 6) Store artifacts CSV + perf traces, push metrics to bench dashboard; 7) Implement regression gate: fail if tokens/sec drop >8% vs baseline or p95 increases >12% for any key workload.
infra_setup: Testbed: 2x and 4x node clusters. Nodes: r4.gpu32 (NVIDIA A100 80GB) with NVLink. Interconnect: 200Gb InfiniBand. OS: Ubuntu 22.04. CUDA 12.1, cuDNN 9.x, NCCL 2.18. Runtime branch: runtime/main as of 2026-02-15. Framework: custom Redwood serving runtime built on top of Triton-style runner + internal kernel dispatcher. Orchestration: systemd services + bench-coordinator script. Time sync: chrony. Benchmark harness container image: ghcr.io/redwood-inference/bench:harness-20260301.
methodology: Workloads: synth and replayed production traces. Sequence lengths: 256/512/2048. Batch regimes: interactive (batch size 1, continuous batching enabled) and throughput (microbatch size 8/16 aggregated into larger kernel batches). For PP: stage count chosen to balance compute across GPUs; for TP: use model sharding with local allreduce for grads disabled (inference-only). For hybrid: pipeline with tensor shards in each stage, microbatching tuned to minimize bubble. Measure steady-state window after KV warmup (skip first 50 tokens). Record tokens/sec (global), p95 token latency per request, GPU SM% and memory alloc/util. Repeat each configuration 5 times and report median and 90% CI.
metrics_definitions: tokens_per_second: global tokens produced by all workers divided by steady-state elapsed seconds; p95_latency_ms: 95th percentile per-request end-to-end latency measured at the client before streaming; gpu_util_percent: average SM% during steady-state; nvlink_bytes_s: aggregate NVLink traffic per second. Regression thresholds: tokens/sec_drop_pct and p95_increase_pct compared to baseline.
run_history: 2026-02-20: Initial harness prototype checked in. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/2198. Basic single-node multi-gpu orchestration works with NCCL allreduce and simple coordinator. Observed noisy p95 on long sequences due to cold KV cache handling.

2026-02-25: Added KV warmup pass and steady-state window trimming to harness. Updated harness image to bench:harness-20260225. Early 4x GPU TP run shows ~3.4x scaling vs single-GPU on seq_len=512 (tokens/sec), pipeline gave ~3.1x. Raw logs uploaded: s3://redwood-bench/ENG-6124/raw-20260225.tar.gz.

2026-03-03: Investigated NVLink saturation on hybrid runs. Added microbatching tuner to reduce pipeline bubbles. Discovered NCCL stress when >64 concurrent connections; mitigated by batching rendezvous. Filed a follow-up ENG-6160 for NCCL tuning in scheduler.

2026-03-09: Formalized regression gate design and integrated with CI bench step. Gate configured to compare to baseline CSV at s3://redwood-bench/bench-baselines/runtime-2.4/ENG-6124-baseline.csv. Alerting wired to slack #bench-alerts and to the bench dashboard: https://dash.redwood.ai/boards/bench-6124.

2026-03-13: Re-ran canonical workloads after kernel update (quant-kernel v2). Hybrid runs decreased tokens/sec by 6.2% on average; under threshold but p95 increased 9% for seq_len=2048 which is within tolerated 12%—marking as In Progress while we validate with a larger sample size. Artifacts: s3://redwood-bench/ENG-6124/results-2026-03-13.csv.
results_summary: Preliminary baselines (median across runs): single A100 80GB baseline tokens/sec for seq_len=512 (throughput regime) = 12,200 tks/s. 4x TP configuration: 41,300 tks/s (~3.39x). 4x PP configuration: 37,900 tks/s (~3.11x). Hybrid 4x (2x pipeline stages x tensor-shard 2) = 74,500 tks/s aggregated for large models (improved memory headroom). p95: single GPU p95=48ms (interactive), 4x-hybrid p95=64ms interactive. Kernel swap (quant-kernel v2) produced a measurable tokens/sec delta -6.2% on hybrid for long sequences; flagged for follow up but under hard regression gate (8%).
regression_detection: Automated gate: compare latest benchmark CSV to baseline. If tokens/sec drops by >8% OR p95 increases by >12% for any canonical workload then fail. Implementation: bench-compare tool (scripts/bench_compare.py) computes relative deltas per workload and uploads a JSON result. CI step 'bench-gate' runs on every runtime PR that touches kernel selection or batching code. Alerts: slack #bench-alerts with link to HTML diff and to perf artifacts. Next step: add anomaly detection to flag persistent drifts across three consecutive runs (to reduce flakiness false positives).
acceptance_criteria: Repeatable harness that can run 1/2/4/8 GPU topologies and persist artifacts to S3
Baseline CSVs captured for canonical workloads (seq_len 256/512/2048 in both interactive and throughput regimes)
CI bench-gate passes on the current runtime/main branch and fails on an intentionally regressed kernel (test case included)
Bench dashboard renders tokens/sec scaling curves and p95 trendlines for all runs
Documentation: runbook describing how to add new workloads and how to interpret regression alerts
